For changesThisMachine (135-139) the method is read from req.method, so a HEAD 'POST route' is not treated as a change route, but no such HEAD handler exists: there are no app.put/app.patch/app.all/app.head routes (grep confirms only get/post/delete), so a POST-route name reached with GET/HEAD/DELETE has no matching handler and falls through the static allowlist to 404. There is no method-override middleware: the only middleware before the routes are express.json at 8, the host/CORS middleware at 115, the loopback gate at 140-148, the ?key= setter at 153 (GET only, line 154), the key gate at 164, the PRIVATE_STATIC filter at 172 and the isPublicPath filter at 206-210; nothing reads X-HTTP-Method-Override or _method (grep for 'override' finds only the redirect at 160).

findings.reasoning: (c) Two dispatch facts together close this: (1) Express 4 (package.json:35 "express": "^4.22.3") matches route patterns against the raw pathname; only captured params are decoded afterwards, so a percent-encoded route literal cannot satisfy it - '/api/local%2Dcat' does not match app.get('/api/local-cat') and never reaches a handler. It instead falls to the static gates: 208 next()s '/api/'-prefixed paths to express.static, which looks for a file named 'local%2Dcat' under an 'api' directory that the allowlist never serves (204-205) and 404s. (2) Should any odd form ever reach a handler, routePath would normalise it exactly as loosely as Express matches: Express is case-insensitive (covered by toLowerCase at 100) and non-strict (trailing slash, covered by replace(/\/+$/, '')) - those are the only liberties Express 4 route matching takes; double slashes ('//api/local-cat') and a dot segment ('/api/./local-cat') do not match the route regexps and are rejected anyway at 203 (empty/'.'/'..' segments) and 175; a semicolon is literal, so '/api/local-cat;x' does not match and also dies at 203/209; the query string is in req.query only, and both routePath and Express routing use req.path, so ?key-test etc. cannot move a path between sets. req.url's raw count is also double-checked by 120 tests on '[a-z0-9_/.%~\-]' hmm - not applicable; the reasoning stands on the two gates.
findings.scenario: Tried without the key: GET /api/local%2Dcat, GET //api/local-cat, GET /api/./local-cat, GET /api/local-cat;x=1, GET /API/Local-CAT/ (the last is the only form that runs a handler, and it is normalised to '/api/local-cat' by 100 and 401s at 167); the first four never reach a handler and end 404 in the static allowlist.
findings.title: Percent-encoded/double-slash/dot/semicolon path forms cannot reach a protected handler

findings.reasoning: OPTIONS is answered 200 at line 123, before the /api cross-site check (124-126) and before the key gate (164-167), so an unauthenticated caller gets 200 on OPTIONS /api/local-cat instead of 401, and any cross-site page gets 200 instead of the cross-site refusal. This is not a data reach: the response is empty (sendStatus), the route handlers never run, Access-Control-Allow-Origin is set only for origins in CORS_ORIGINS (120, allowlist built at 27-28), and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is never set, so a foreign page still cannot read protected responses; it merely reveals that a ViewAlign server with those endpoints exists. The preflight answer is needed so the CORS_ORIGINS pages (line 27) can use the API.
findings.scenario: Case covered: OPTIONS /api/local-cat without the key from a random origin -> 200 with no CORS grant and no body; following GET still 401. No protected route's handler runs for OPTIONS, so the wrong result is limited to a friendlier probe answer than 404/401 would be.
findings.title: OPTIONS answers 200 for every path before the key and cross-site checks, without any data

findings.reasoning: Even with the key in hand, this delete only removes registered entries: 860 returns 404 unless the name is a key of DATABASES (so '/api/blast-db/..' or a name never added by the owner deletes nothing), and every unlink is guarded by isOwnedDbFile at 872 and 874-875, so only index/database files inside blast_dbs/ are actually removed - a database registered from elsewhere is unregistered, not deleted (868-869). Stepping backwards through slashes: DELETE /api/blast-db//x does not match Express (extra segment) and dies 404 in static; DELETE /api/blast-db/x%2f stays raw and still startsWith('/api/blast-db/'), so it is refused anyway.
